{{Quote|One of these smugglers is my mark. I think. I'm not sure. I've been tracking him for some time and just now caught up with him here in this city.|[[Tearfin]], to a spacer|<ref name="SWG:TMotH" />}}
'''D'lonis''' was a [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Smuggler/Legends|smuggler]] who lived during the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]].

==Biography==
{{Quote|The guy I'm looking for stole some equipment. Nobody got a good look at him, but the crate that he stole had a transponder signal attached to it.|Tearfin, to a spacer|<ref name="SWG:TMotH" />}}
In [[1 ABY/Legends|1 ABY]],<ref name="SWG_timeline">{{SWG_timeline}}</ref> D'lonis was present on [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]], visiting several [[City/Legends|cities]] on the planet. At the same time, a [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunter]] named [[Tearfin]] traveled to the planet. The bounty hunter was seeking a [[Smuggler/Legends|smuggler]] who stole a crate of valuable equipment. As the crate had a [[transponder]], she easily traced her mark to Tatooine. However, the thief found the transponder and turned it off not long after Tearfin arrived on the planet. The bounty hunter then located D'lonis and a group of smugglers, suspecting one of them of being her mark, but she was not able to identify the thief. Besides D'lonis, the group included five other smugglers, namely [[Parugga]], [[Rh'klin]], [[Barosk]], [[Klaphini]] and [[Captain/Legends|Captain]] [[Himfan]]. Tearfin interrogated D'lonis and the other smugglers, but could not determine who was innocent or guilty, basically because all of the smugglers simply blamed each other. A [[Spacer/Legends|spacer]] seeking to [[Quest of the Hero of Tatooine|become]] a [[Hero of Tatooine]] eventually came along to help Tearfin. After interrogating all the smugglers, the spacer finally identified the thief. The spacer later informed Tearfin and was awarded the [[Mark of Intellect]] for the successful investigation.<ref name="SWG:TMotH" />

==Behind the scenes==
[[File:FileTemplateSmuggler.jpg|250px|thumb|Every possible depictions of D'lonis]]
D'lonis was a [[Wikipedia:Non-player character|non-player character]] (NPC) in the [[2003]] [[Star Wars video games|video game]] ''[[Star Wars Galaxies]]'', a [[Wikipedia:Massively multiplayer online role-playing game|massively multiplayer online roleplaying game]] developed by [[Sony]] Online Entertainment and published by [[LucasArts]],<ref name="SWG">{{GalaxiesAED}}</ref> prior to its closure on [[December 15]], [[2011]].<ref name="Shutdown">{{SonyCite|url=playerinfo|text=IMPORTANT INFORMATION ABOUT ''STAR WARS'' GALAXIES™}}</ref> Because D'lonis spawned under the generic "smuggler" template, the appearance of this NPC was randomized under one of eight possible depictions.<ref name="SWG" />

D'lonis was added to the game as part of the [[W:c:swg:Hero of Tatooine|"Hero of Tatooine" questline]],<ref name="SWG" /> released with "[[W:c:swg:Publish 9 Notes for 29 June 04|Publish 9]]" on [[June 29]], [[2004]].<ref>{{SonyCite|url=recent_updates.jsp?page=Recent%20Updates|text=Publish 9 Secrets of the Force}}</ref> This NPC periodically spawned in random cities across Tatooine, along with Tearfin and the five other smugglers. Players taking part in the "Intellect" segment of the "Hero of Tatooine" had to interrogate D'lonis and the other smugglers to determine which one was Tearfin's mark. The identity of the culprit varied among the six smugglers each time the quest was reset.<ref name="SWG" /> With the release of the "[[W:c:swg:Publish 24|Publish 24]]," on [[October 18]], [[2005]], D'lonis and the five other smugglers were given proper names<ref name="SWG-2005">{{SonyCite|url=players/content.vm?id=64886&resource=publish|text=Publish Archive 2005}}</ref> to replace randomly generated names.<ref name="SWG" />

The "Hero of Tatooine" questline was extensively revamped upon the introduction of the "[[W:c:swg:Publish 25 Notes for November 15, 2005|Publish 25]]," a.k.a. the "[[W:c:swg:New Game Enhancements|New Game Enhancements]]," on [[November 15]], [[2005]]<ref name="SWG-2005" /> but the "Intellect" segment was not altered.<ref name="SWG:TMotH" />
